extracted.intended_audience: law students, patent practitioners, and judges (U.S. patent law)
extracted.subtask_description: Index and table-of-contents excerpt from a U.S. patent law textbook summarizing key doctrines, procedural rules, and substantive standards used to evaluate patent applications, validity, infringement, remedies, and prosecution practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment (application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of application; abandonment of (general) (index references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural topic: how and when an application is considered abandoned; related entry references include application abandonment at pages 19 and elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation (novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic novelty requirement: prior art that anticipates a claimed invention renders it unpatentable. (Index cross-references to discussion at pages 52, 60.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure duty requiring disclosure of the best mode known to the inventor at time of filing. (See discussion at 72–73.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement (section 112 enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement requires disclosure sufficient to 'make and carry out' and 'to use' the invention; considers the hypothetical person skilled in the art, timing, and undue experimentation. (References: pages 16, 70–72; hypothetical person: 71; undue experimentation: 71–72.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written description doctrine as part of Section 112 disclosure obligations; tied to enablement and best mode (see pages 69–73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction — includes terms like 'comprising' and 'consisting of' and general claim-construction principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules and principles for interpreting claim language; construction affects infringement and validity analyses. (Index references: pages 11–12, 80.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim types (independent/dependent/multiple-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent and independent claims; multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification of claim forms and their drafting/interpretation consequences. (Index: dependent, independent, multiple dependent — pages 12, 11–12.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function (35 U.S.C. §112) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Means-plus-function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims drafted in means-plus-function format are governed by Section 112/112(f) rules constraining the scope to corresponding structure in the specification. (References: pages 80, 81–82.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Product-by-process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product-by-process claim form and its implications for infringement and validity analysis. (See pages 73, 81.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for rejection of claims (prosecution grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims — basis for rejection, generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds on which examiners reject claims during prosecution (e.g., anticipation, obviousness, lack of enablement/written description, new matter). (Index: pages 15–16.)

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter (amendment restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment — new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments adding new matter are prohibited; doctrine governs what can be added during prosecution or by amendment. (Index: amendment new matter, pages 17, 69.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and good faith / information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty of candor and good faith; information disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and counsel must disclose material prior art and information to the PTO; failure can lead to inequitable conduct. (Index: duty of candor and good faith, pages 11, 91; information disclosure statement, page 11.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct (standards for misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inequitable conduct; fraud on the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: clear and convincing evidence of intent to mislead and materiality; cumulative information considerations; gross negligence insufficient; intent may be inferred; PTO materiality standard referenced. (Index references: pages 89–92; clarity: page 90–92; cumulative info and gross negligence: 91.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (35 U.S.C. §103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness-type (double patenting) and section 103 obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness analysis under Section 103 and related double-patenting concerns; includes the legal standard for unpatentability for obvious combinations. (Index: pages 16, 59, 61.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents (DOE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrine of equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests and limits for DOE including the function/way/result test, hypothetical claim analysis, range of equivalents, reverse doctrine of equivalents, and limitations such as prosecution history estoppel. (Index references: pages 80, 82–84; function/way/result test: 82; hypothetical claim analysis: 83; range of equivalents: 83; reverse doctrine: 84; prosecution history estoppel: 83–84.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution history estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution history estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the application of the doctrine of equivalents based on amendments or arguments made during prosecution (see pages 83–84).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement (elements and types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement — elements generally; direct, contributory, inducing, literal infringement; acts include making, using, offering to sell, selling, or importing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements to prove infringement depend on claim scope and type (product vs process); statutory acts listed; distinctions among direct, literal, contributory, and induced infringement. (Index references: pages 75–79, 80–82, 76.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory infringement (elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributory infringement — knowledge; noninfringing use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires knowledge and that the accused product has no substantial noninfringing uses; related defenses and analyses elaborated. (Index: pages 77–79, 85; knowledge: 78–79; noninfringing use: 78.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inducing infringement (intent requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inducing infringement — intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability for inducement requires intent to cause infringement; evaluated in context of knowledge and actions encouraging infringement. (Index: inducing infringement pages 77, 78–79, 85; intent: 79.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Literal infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal infringement (claim elements match exactly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis comparing accused product/practice to the claim language as construed. (Index: pages 80–82.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exceptions and territorial limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory exceptions and territorial limits on infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain acts or circumstances fall outside infringement (e.g., experimental use, statutory exemptions); also territoriality (imports) and limits of U.S. law. (Index: statutory exceptions pages 75, 85; territorial limits: pages 84–86; imports: 84–85.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages — types and calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages — compensatory, lost profits, reasonable royalty, mixed awards, interest, punitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for calculating lost profits and reasonable royalties, marking requirements for damages, mixed awards, prejudgment and postjudgment interest, and punitive damages/ increased damages. (Index: pages 97, 105–11, 111–15, 115–16, 123–26, 118.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lost profits and entire market value rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Lost profits; entire market value rule; market-share analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods for proving lost profits (e.g., Panduit test), when entire market value rule applies, and use of market-share analyses. (Index: lost profits pages 105–11; entire market value rule page 109; market-share analysis page 108.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable royalty as a damages measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework and factors for establishing a reasonable royalty; interplay with lost profits, marking, and mixed awards. (Index: pages 111–15; marking referenced 116–17.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased damages / willful infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased damages — willful infringement and factors for increased damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may award enhanced damages for willful infringement; factors and standards for willfulness and enhanced awards discussed. (Index: increased damages pages 117–21; willful infringement pages 118–20; factors: 118.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney's fees (exceptional cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney’s fees — exceptional case, calculating, lodestar amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for awarding fees to prevailing parties in exceptional cases and calculation methods such as the lodestar approach. (Index: attorney’s fees pages 121–23; exceptional case 121–22; lodestar amount 122.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions (preliminary and permanent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Injunctions — historical, preliminary, permanent, and stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for preliminary and permanent injunctive relief in patent cases, historical context, and rules for stays of injunctions. (Index: pages 97–104; preliminary 98–101; permanent 101–02; stays 102–04.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable defenses (laches, estoppel, misuse, unclean hands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable defenses — equitable estoppel, laches, patent misuse, unclean hands, inequitable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various equitable defenses that can bar relief or affect remedies; each has elements and burdens addressed in the text. (Index: pages 89–96 (inequitable conduct, equitable estoppel, laches, patent misuse, unclean hands).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable estoppel (elements and burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable estoppel — elements, burden of proof, types of prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements include misleading conduct, reliance, material prejudice (economic and evidentiary); burden of proof and consequence (no injunction). (Index: equitable estoppel pages 95–96; burden of proof 96; elements 95–96; types of prejudice: economic 96, evidentiary 96; misleading conduct: 95; reliance: 95; no injunction: 95.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches (delay and prejudice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laches — delay, prejudice, diligence, excuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements include unreasonable delay and resulting prejudice; considerations of diligence and excuses, effect on injunctions and damages (pages 93–95; diligence 94; delay 94; prejudice 94).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference proceedings and priority (diligence/reduction to practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interference — appeals, diligence, reduction to practice, conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-AIA interferences legacy rules: priority disputes, required proofs of diligence and conception/reduction to practice. (Index: interference pages 23–24, 57–58; appeals 26; diligence 24, 57.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing date and priority (foreign priority, effective filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date; effective filing date; foreign priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance of filing date for novelty/priority; foreign priority rules and effective filing concepts. (Index: filing date pages 9, 13, 22–23; effective filing 23; foreign priority 22–23.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation practice (continuation, continuation-in-part, divisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation, continuation-in-part, divisional applications; copending and serial relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different continuation filings, their purposes, and effects on priority/claim scope. (Index: continuation pages 19–21; copending 20; divisional 21; continuation-in-part 20–21.)

rubrics_metrics.name: File wrapper / prosecution history
rubrics_metrics.description: File wrapper (prosecution history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance of the prosecution record in claim construction, estoppel, and litigation (index reference page 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures and examiners (historical PTO procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination — 1790, 1793, 1836 procedures; examiners (assistant, primary, supervisory primary, group director) and examining groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural history and organization of patent examination; roles of different examiners and historical procedures guiding modern practice. (Index: examination pages 2–3, 8, 1790/1793/1836 references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction (Federal Circuit and subject/personal jurisdiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Circuit jurisdiction; 'arising under' subject matter jurisdiction and personal jurisdiction issues (including stream-of-commerce and well-pleaded complaint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate jurisdiction of the Federal Circuit, jurisdictional tests for patent cases, and procedural routes for appeals. (Index: Federal Circuit pages 3, 25–26, 26, 47; jurisdiction pages 36–37.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship and conception/reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor topics — conception, reduced to practice, joint inventors, deceased/insane/incapacitated inventors, misjoinder/nonjoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for inventorship, corrections of inventorship, legal effect of inventor status, and historical concepts of exclusive rights. (Index: inventor pages 8, 9, 23–24, 53–54, 64.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking (for damages) and notice to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Marking — notice and its effect on damages (post-filing damages, marking requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory and case-law rules on marking products with patent numbers to preserve damages entitlement; interaction with lost-profits and royalty calculations. (Index: marking pages 116–17; post-filing damages 95.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire market value / market-share analysis (damages proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entire market value rule and market-share analysis as methods in damages calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances where patentee may recover damages measured by the value of the entire product versus only the patented feature; use of market-share methods. (Index: entire market value rule page 109; market-share analysis page 108.)
